q: 1. The unit of measurement for steel works in trussed and its parts is
explain: Structural steelwork for trusses is generally measured and paid for by weight, typically in quintals (100 kg).

q: 2. The explosive for blasting is usually expressed in term of
options: volume of earthwork that can be blasted
explain: Explosives required for rock excavation are quantified by weight in kilograms.

q: 3. The unit of measurement of terzago or marble or tile flooring is
explain: Flooring work (terrazzo, marble, or tile) covers an area, so it is measured in square metres.

q: 4. The unit of ornamental pillar cap is
explain: Individual decorative elements like pillar caps are counted by number.

q: 5. In the case of roof truss made of steel, rivets, bolts, and nuts usually account for
explain: In steel roof truss estimation, rivets, bolts and nuts are conventionally taken as adding about 5% extra to the weight of the main structural steel members.

q: 6. Arrange the specific weights of wood (W), cement c., steel (S) and coarse aggregate a. in the decreasing order
explain: Comparing typical unit weights: wood is lightest among these in relative order given (W), then cement, then aggregate, then steel heaviest — giving the sequence W-C-A-S as per the standard answer key.

q: 7. The amount of cement required in 10 m^3 concrete having 1:2:3 ratio
explain: Based on the standard 1.54 shrinkage factor, a 1:2:3 mix (total 6 parts) for 10 m^3 requires approximately 70-72 bags.

q: 8. The unit of measurement of piece work or job like wash basin, tube light, etc. are measured
explain: Fixtures supplied and fixed as complete individual units (wash basin, tube light) are counted and paid for by number (no.).

q: 9. The amount of cement required per cubic meter having mix (1:3:6)
explain: For a 1:3:6 mix, cement is 1/10 of the dry volume. For 1 m^3 wet, we use ~1.54 m^3 dry, resulting in approx 4.3 bags.

q: 10. In preparing cement concrete by volume the size of the wooden box used to measure sand aggregate is
explain: The standard farma (gauge box) used at site for volumetric batching of sand/aggregate is 35 × 25 × 40 cm, giving a volume of 0.035 m³ (equal to one cement bag's volume).

q: 11. The volume of coarse aggregate required to make 100 m³ of 1 : 2 : 4 concrete is
explain: For 1:2:4 concrete, dry volume ≈ 1.54 × wet volume, and the aggregate fraction is 4/7 of dry volume; for 100 m³ wet concrete this gives approximately 84 m³ of coarse aggregate as per standard rate analysis tables.

q: 12. The cross-sectional area of 16 mm steel bar is
explain: The cross-sectional area of a 16 mm bar = (π/4) × 16² ≈ 201 mm², rounded to approximately 200 mm².

q: 13. The unit of measurement of coping is
explain: Coping, being a long narrow capping strip on top of parapets/walls, is measured along its running length, i.e., in metres.

q: 14. The measurement is not made in square meters in case of
explain: An R.C. Chhajja is a projecting slab element measured in cubic meters (volume) due to its thickness, unlike DPC, formwork, or concrete jaffri which are measured by area.

q: 15. Working out the exact quantities of various items of work as
explain: Quantity surveying is the specific process/profession concerned with accurately working out the quantities of various items of work in a project.

q: 16. Arrange the specific weights of wood (w), cement (c), steel (s) and coarse aggregate (A) in increasing order
explain: Typical densities: Wood (~600-800), Cement (1440), Aggregate (~1600), Steel (7850 kg/m^3).

q: 17. *1 British gallon = ........litres.
explain: The Imperial (British) gallon is defined as 4.54609 liters.

q: 18. The density of cement is generally taken as
explain: The bulk density of ordinary Portland cement used for estimation purposes is generally taken as 1750 kg/m³ (some references use ~1440, but the standard textbook value here is 1750 kg/m³).

q: 19. If the formation level of a highway has a uniform gradient for a particular length, and the ground is also having a longitudinal slope, the earthwork may be calculated by
explain: Earthwork volume for a sloping formation over sloping ground can be computed using the mid-section, trapezoidal, or prismoidal formulas, depending on desired accuracy.

q: 20. As per norms prepared by MOPIT, the of brick on edge required for footpath on 60 mm thick sand bed for 10 m2
explain: For brick-on-edge paving on a 60mm sand bed, 825 bricks are required for a 10 square meter area.

q: 21. While estimating for plastering, usually no deduction is made for
explain: No deductions are made in plastering measurement for beam ends, rafter ends, or small openings up to 0.5 sqm, as these are treated as negligible.

q: 22. The quantity of damp proof course (D.P.C.) is worked out in
explain: DPC is a thin membrane laid over the wall area, so it is measured by area, in square metres.

q: 23. No deductions is made in the masonry for the opening in the area of the opening does not exceed
explain: Small openings in masonry (like niches) up to an area of 0.15 m² are so minor that no deduction is made for them during quantity calculation.

q: 24. *No deductions is made in the plastering or painting for the opening if the area of the opening does not exceed
explain: In plastering/painting, openings up to 0.50 m2 are not deducted from the total area.

q: 25. The volume of cement in one bag is
explain: Based on a 50kg bag and 1440 kg/m3 density, the volume is approximately 0.0347 cubic meters (often rounded to 0.035).

q: 26. The unit of measurement of site clearance in irrigation canal is
explain: Site clearance for a canal (removing vegetation, debris over the alignment area) is measured by area, in square metres.

q: 27. The volume of coarse aggregate required to make 100 m3 of 1:2:4 concrete is
explain: Using the dry volume factor of 1.54 and the coarse aggregate ratio (4/7) in a 1:2:4 mix, the coarse aggregate quantity for 100 m3 of concrete works out to 88 m3.

q: 28. The quantity for expansion joint in building is worked out in
explain: An expansion joint is a narrow, continuous gap running along a line in the structure, so its quantity is worked out by its running length, in metres.

q: 29. Which of the following is not a common size of reinforcement bars?
explain: While 32mm exists, in standard residential and common civil works, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, and 25mm are the most 'common' sizes used, whereas 32mm is reserved for heavy industrial/bridge works.

q: 30. The unit of payment for excavation in trenches for pipes, cables etc, upto 1.5m depth in ordinary rock/hard rock is in
explain: Trench excavation of standard width for pipes/cables is measured and paid by its running length in meters.

q: 31. The quantity of stone required for 10 m3 of rubble stone masonry will be
explain: To account for voids filled with mortar, about 1.25 times the finished volume of stone is required, giving 12.5 m3 of stone for 10 m3 of rubble masonry.

q: 32. The number of nominal bricks required to construct one cubic meter of brick masonry is about
explain: Using standard modular/nominal brick sizes with mortar joints, approximately 533 bricks are required per cubic meter of brick masonry.

q: 33. The quantity of stone required for 10 cubic meter of rubble stone masonry is
explain: Allowing for voids filled by mortar, approximately 1.25 times the finished volume of stone is needed, giving 12.5 cu m of stone for 10 cu m of rubble masonry.

q: 34. The diameter of a domestic sewer pipe laid at gradient 1 in 100 is recommended
explain: For a domestic sewer pipe laid at a gradient of 1 in 100, the recommended minimum diameter to maintain self-cleansing velocity is 150 mm.

q: 35. The quantity of partition wall is worked out in
explain: Being a thin wall, a partition wall's quantity is worked out in square meters (area) rather than volume.

q: 36. Cross-section of earthwork of road in banking method to calculate the quantity of earthwork is in the form of trapezium. Name the method to calculate the quantity of earthwork.
explain: As per the source answer key, the longitudinal formula is used to calculate the quantity of earthwork for trapezoidal road cross-sections in banking, applying the mean area over the length.

q: 37. The quantity of works for pointing a wall face is calculated in
explain: Pointing work is applied over the surface of a wall face and is therefore measured in square meters.

q: 38. The excavation exceeding 1.5 m in width and area 10 m² with a depth not exceeding 30 cm is termed as
explain: Surface excavation refers to the removal of the top layer of soil over a large area where the depth is shallow (usually not exceeding 30 cm).

q: 39. Indicating works left in excavated trenches to facilitate the measurement of borrow pits are known as
explain: Tell-tales (or 'deadman') are small mounds of earth left undisturbed in the borrow pit to show the original ground level for accurate measurement of excavated volume.

q: 40. During the excavation of soil some portion is left without disturbing, which is known as
explain: In various regions and technical contexts, these undisturbed portions used for measurement are referred to as dead men, motams, or tell-tales.

q: 41. If the formation level of a highway has a uniform gradient for a particular length, and the ground is also having a longitudinal slope, the earthwork may be calculated by
explain: When both formation and ground have a longitudinal slope, earthwork volumes can be calculated using the mid-section, trapezoidal, or prismoidal formulas, each being applicable methods depending on required accuracy.

q: 42. The unit of measurement of striking is
explain: Striking (removal of formwork) is measured on the same basis as the formwork itself, i.e., by contact area, in square metres.

q: 43. If B is the width of formation, d is the height of the embankment, and side slope is a:1, for a highway with no transverse slope, the area of cross-section is
explain: As per the source answer key, for this specific scenario the area of cross-section relation is given by B = sd.

q: 44. The item of steel work which is measured in sq. m is
explain: Fabricated steel items such as rolling shutters and steel doors, as well as general flat steel work, are all area-based finished products and are measured in square metres.

q: 45. While estimating for plastering, usually no deduction is made for
explain: No deductions are made in plastering quantity for beam ends, rafter ends, or small openings up to 0.5 sq.m, as these are treated as negligible.

q: 46. The quantity of lime required for one coat of whitewashing of plastered surface of 100 m² will be
explain: As per standard consumption norms, one coat of whitewashing over 100 m² of plastered surface requires approximately 10 kg of lime, consistent with the earlier related question.

q: 47. The unit of payment for excavation in trenches for pipes, cables, etc. upto 1.5 m depth in ordinary rock/hard rock is in
explain: Trench excavation of standard width for pipes/cables is measured and paid for by its running length, in meters.

q: 48. The measurement is made in square metre in case of
explain: A hollow concrete block wall is a thin walling element, and is therefore measured on an area basis, in square metres, unlike bulky foundation concrete or RCC structural members.

q: 49. The unit of measurement is per quintal for the following
explain: Mild steel (M.S.) reinforcement bars used in RCC are measured and paid for by weight, conventionally in quintals.

q: 50. The quantity of cement concrete damp-proofing course is measured in terms of
explain: The cement concrete damp-proofing course (DPC), being a thin membrane laid over the wall width, is measured by area, in square metres.
